summary:
AstroCore (C.O.R.E.) is an autonomous, localized crew bio-telemetry platform designed to prevent the interconnected physiological hazards of deep-space travel: cardiovascular deconditioning and acute kidney stone formation.
Developed by a cross-functional team of cardiologists, a nephrologist, and a finance risk-modeling lead, the platform addresses the health-monitoring challenge by shifting space medicine from reactive treatment to predictive prevention. AstroCore passively ingests data from wearable ECG patches, exercise logs, and automated spacecraft waste-management sensors. Using a localized Python Flask microservice running entirely on the spacecraft’s internal network—requiring zero Earth-cloud connectivity during deep-space communication blackouts—the engine calculates real-time Dynamic Risk and Orthostatic Tolerance indices.
Calibrated against peer-reviewed NASA Life Sciences Data Archive benchmarks (Experiments DSO 621, DSO 462, and Apollo AP004), AstroCore classifies astronaut adaptation phenotypes within 72 hours of launch and delivers actionable, closed-loop hydration and countermeasure prescriptions. This technology is vital because a single renal colic episode or landing-day blackout could incapacitate a Mars transit crew and compromise a multi-billion-dollar mission, while its hot-swappable Earth mode simultaneously protects isolated terrestrial workers from six-figure emergency medical evacuations.
details:
AstroCore (C.O.R.E. – Cardio-Orthostatic & Renal Engine) is an autonomous, localized crew bio-telemetry platform that monitors, predicts, and prevents the interconnected risks of cardiovascular deconditioning and acute kidney stone formation (nephrolithiasis) during long-duration spaceflight.

The platform operates through a three-layer closed-loop architecture:

  1. Autonomous Telemetry Ingestion: AstroCore passively collects real-time biometric data from wearable ECG/HRV patches, exercise equipment logs (ARED resistance and cardio metrics), and conceptual in-line spacecraft waste-management sensors that analyze urine specific gravity, pH, calcium, and sodium concentrations.
  2. Multi-Mode Predictive Analytics Engine: A localized Python Flask microservice processes these biomarkers into two real-time risk scores on a 0–100 scale: the Dynamic Risk Index (DRI) for renal crystallization and the Orthostatic Tolerance Index (OTI) for landing-day blackout (syncope) risk. The engine forecasts physiological trajectories up to 14 days in advance.
  3. Closed-Loop Actionable Interventions: Rather than displaying raw clinical numbers, the low-glare cockpit dashboard translates risk alerts into immediate, hyper-specific countermeasures—such as exact milliliter hydration windows, dietary sodium limits, or Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) vacuum pod adjustments—while compressing data bursts for Earth-based flight surgeons.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Deep-Space Crew Autonomy: Because missions to Mars face up to 20-minute communication delays with Earth, AstroCore runs entirely on the spacecraft’s internal local area network (LAN) without requiring cloud connectivity, giving crews immediate medical decision support.
  • Preventative Mission Protection: A single painful kidney stone episode or landing-day fainting event can incapacitate an astronaut and compromise a multi-billion-dollar mission. AstroCore shifts aerospace medicine from reactive emergency treatment to proactive, personalized prevention.
  • Dual-Use Earth Scalability: By hot-swapping its configuration matrix from SPACE mode to EARTH mode, the exact same software architecture recalibrates to monitor environmental heat stress and severe dehydration in extreme terrestrial industries (offshore oil rigs, deep mining, maritime shipping, and rural clinics). Preventing just one emergency terrestrial medical evacuation ($150,000+ average cost) yields over a 250% annual return on investment.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Backend & Analytics Engine: Python 3, Flask REST API, and modular object-oriented configuration matrices (config.py) processing structured JSON telemetry schemas.
  • Frontend & Visualization: Interactive UI simulation widgets, dark-mode aerospace cockpit styling (#0B0F19 palette), and dynamic risk gauges.
  • NASA Open Data Archives: Calibrated directly against peer-reviewed datasets from the NASA Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA), including Experiment DSO 621 (re-entry arterial pressure and stroke volume drops), Experiment DSO 462 (central venous pressure adaptation phenotypes), and Apollo 7–17 Dataset AP004 (post-flight urinary biochemistry).
  • AI & Development Tooling: Co-developed using Google AI for dataset synthesis, physiological-to-algorithmic parameter balancing, and financial modeling, alongside CodeRick AI for JSON schema structuring, code optimization, and documentation compilation.

What Makes Our Project Creative

  • Phenotype-Driven Personalization: While analyzing NASA LSDA Experiment DSO 462, our team recognized that astronauts do not adapt to microgravity uniformly—crews diverge into Increasing CVP and Decreasing CVP subgroups by Flight Day 3–4 (\(p = 0.0321\)). AstroCore creatively incorporates an early-flight Phenotype Classifier that identifies an astronaut's specific adaptation profile within 72 hours and customizes their fluid and LBNP countermeasure targets accordingly.
  • Post-Mission Re-Adaptation Tracking: Using historical Apollo AP004 telemetry, we discovered that kidney stone risk actually spikes after splashdown—driven by a 49.2% drop in urine volume at +24 hours and a delayed 33.3% surge in calcium excretion at +6 days. AstroCore includes a dedicated EARTH_RE_ADAPTATION mode to protect returning crews during their first week back in gravity.
  • Cross-Disciplinary Team Synergy: Our solution uniquely combines practicing clinical expertise (Dr. Atul Maini, Nephrologist; Dr. Mansi Maini, Cardiologist) with quantitative financial risk modeling (Manav Maini, Indiana University Kelley School of Business Finance Major).

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Connected Organ Physiology: We designed the heart and kidney modules as a single linked system rather than isolated trackers, modeling how upward fluid shifts in zero gravity trigger renal water dumping, blood volume loss, and concentrated urinary calcium saturation.
  • Cognitive Load Under Stress: Astronauts operate under intense mental workloads, so we engineered a high-contrast dark interface with color-coded triage tiers (Nominal, Elevated, Critical) that can be interpreted in under two seconds.
  • Scientific Precision Between Space and Earth: Rather than applying microgravity bone-loss equations directly to Earth workers, our team built a modular configuration dictionary so the engine accurately separates zero-gravity hypercalciuria from terrestrial thermal sweat dehydration.
